title: Darfur Governor Minawi Leads Sudanese Delegation to Juba, Seeks Renewed South Sudan Mediation
detail: A Sudanese delegation led by Darfur Regional Governor Mini Arko Minawi met South Sudanese President Salva Kiir Mayardit in Juba on or around August 18, 2026, recalling Kiir's past mediation role in Sudan's civil war and calling for renewed focus on implementing the 2020 Juba Peace Agreement. Discussions covered regional stability, security arrangements and joint forces, and the ethnic and demographic dimensions of the conflict in Darfur. Kiir said 'Peace in South Sudan is the peace of Sudan, and the stability of Sudan is the stability of South Sudan,' and the two sides agreed South Sudan would send a presidential delegation to Khartoum to assess implementation gaps in the Juba accord. The visit follows South Sudan's continued positioning as a potential mediator between SAF and RSF, alongside the AU Peace and Security Council's August 16 Khartoum visit and the African Union's broader push for a Sudanese-led political settlement.

media.caption: Darfur Governor Mini Arko Minawi's delegation met South Sudan's President Salva Kiir in Juba around August 18, 2026, seeking renewed mediation on Sudan's war.

confidenceReason: Reported by a single South Sudanese outlet with direct quotes; not yet independently corroborated by Sudanese or international wire coverage at time of writing.

title: UNIDO Unveils Roadmap for Sudan's Industrial Recovery, Plans September Investment Mission
detail: The UN Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO) laid out a roadmap on August 18, 2026 for shifting Sudan from traditional post-war reconstruction toward sustainable economic recovery, emphasizing rebuilding value and production chains, job creation, and expansion of the private sector, with small and medium enterprises identified as key growth drivers. The plan includes establishing an Industrial Recovery Fund to mobilize financing. UNIDO Director-General Gerd Müller said 'the time has come to move from discussions and conferences to practical implementation.' UNIDO is organizing an investment mission to Sudan for September 5-11, 2026, bringing European and German companies and international financing and development institutions to identify investment opportunities and build partnerships with Sudan's private sector. Separately, Sudanese Employers' Federation representative Muhannad Awad said addressing gold smuggling — a major RSF revenue source — requires 'creating economic incentives that make keeping gold within Sudan more profitable than smuggling it.'

sources.name: Sudan Horizon — UNIDO Lays Out a Roadmap for Economic and Industrial Recovery in Sudan
